guarantees.claim: When hmac_en_i is true, sha_hash_start_o routes the internal hash_start signal; otherwise it passes reg_hash_start_i directly.
sha_hash_continue_o is hash_continue when hmac_en_i is true, else reg_hash_continue_i.
sha_hash_process_o is (reg_hash_process_i | hash_process) when hmac_en_i is true, else reg_hash_process_i alone.
hash_done_o is hmac_hash_done when hmac_en_i is true, else sha_hash_done_i.
pad_index_512 is assigned as bit slice txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA512-1:HashWordBitsSHA256].
pad_index_256 is assigned as bit slice txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA256-1:HashWordBitsSHA256].

assumptions.claim: When hmac_en_i is true, the internal signals hash_start, hash_continue, hash_process, hmac_hash_done, and txcount must be correctly driven by the state machine not shown in this chunk.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect HMAC sequencing can lead to wrong hash operations or data corruption.

assumptions.claim: In bypass mode (hmac_en_i=0), the external reg_hash_start_i, reg_hash_continue_i, reg_hash_process_i, and sha_hash_done_i must form a valid, non‑conflicting SHA‑2 operation sequence.
assumptions.risk: Glitch or spurious hash_done/start/continue signals could cause the SHA engine to misbehave or enter an unexpected state.

assumptions.claim: txcount must never exceed a value that causes pad_index_512 or pad_index_256 to index beyond the declared dimensions of i_pad_256/i_pad_512/o_pad_256/o_pad_512 arrays.
assumptions.cond: when HMAC state machine uses txcount to generate pad indices
assumptions.risk: Out‑of‑bounds read from pad arrays could expose secret key bytes (XORed with ipad/opad) to the data path, violating key secrecy.

uncertain_points.claim: The chunks that use pad_index_512/pad_index_256 to index i_pad_256/i_pad_512/o_pad_256/o_pad_512 arrays may lack bounds checking; an out‑of‑range index could read secret key material.
uncertain_points.cond: When HMAC is active and txcount is incremented beyond the safe word count.
uncertain_points.risk: Secret key leakage on the HMAC data output or into the hash engine.

uncertain_points.claim: Bypass mode (hmac_en_i=0) directly passes external control signals to the SHA engine without any clearing of HMAC‑internal key state or forced idle transition; residual key material from a previous HMAC operation could contaminate the bypass hash or be leaked.
uncertain_points.cond: When hmac_en_i transitions from 1 to 0 or the core is reused after an HMAC computation.
uncertain_points.risk: Key material might be inferable through timing or data correlations in subsequent bypass hashes.
